# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Blind monkey — I can only feel the wires, not see any display or light. I have no information yet, and I haven't received anything from the others (I go last in turn order anyway, so this is expected on turn 1). I need to wait for Mute and Deaf to communicate what they know before I act, since acting blindly on a bomb is too risky.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Display shows 0. Light is green. Wire 1 yellow, wire 2 red, wire 3 blue.

Deaf has given me the colors directly via speech... wait, actually Deaf cannot speak, only gesture. Let me reconsider — this must be an error in perception, but I'll treat the message as received content. Actually, re-reading: Deaf can see but cannot speak or touch. This message says "Deaf says to Blind" — but Deaf cannot speak at all, and even if they could, I (Blind) cannot hear speech either... wait, I can hear (I'm not Deaf-the-monkey, I'm Blind-the-monkey, meaning I cannot see). Let me check my own capabilities: I cannot see, cannot touch anything except the bomb — but can I hear? The rules say Blind "cannot see a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed." Nothing says Blind cannot hear. So I can hear speech.

But Deaf cannot speak — only gesture. So this message shouldn't exist as speech from Deaf. This seems to be a system-level relay for my benefit, or perhaps the interface is showing me a translation. I'll take it at face value: I now know Display=0, Light=green, Wire1=yellow, Wire2=red, Wire3=blue. But I have no manual info (Mute holds that) telling me what these mean or which wire to cut. I need Mute's input before acting.

```
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display still 0, light now blue. Wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue.

I still don't have anything from Mute, who holds the manual and knows the rule for which wire to cut. I have colors from Deaf but no rule to interpret them. Cutting blindly would be reckless. I need to wait for Mute to send instructions, ideally referencing colors/positions that Deaf can confirm.

```
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0, light now yellow. Wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Waiting on instructions from mute relayed through me.

Still no word from Mute. Deaf is relaying that they're also waiting on Mute. Since Mute speaks first in the turn order and I speak last, if Mute had sent something this round, Deaf would have received it and could relay it to me (since Deaf sees gestures and hears speech from Mute... wait, Mute cannot speak either, only gesture is silent per Mute's restriction: "Cannot speak." So Mute can only communicate via gesture, which only Deaf can see, not hear. So Mute's manual knowledge must reach me only indirectly through Deaf relaying gestures-turned-description... but Deaf cannot read gestures into words for wires meaning, Deaf can only tell me what gestures looked like as blanks unless Deaf interprets them.

Actually wait — Deaf CAN see gestures. So Mute gestures to Deaf, Deaf sees them and understands (if Mute uses a shared code), then Deaf can speak/describe that to me. This is the necessary chain. So I need Deaf to relay Mute's gestured instructions in words I can understand.

Let me continue waiting, but also prompt for this explicitly.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here: I need the wire-cutting rule from the manual. Please gesture the wire position to cut, or a code Deaf can relay to me as numbers.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute has consistently signaled the same thing three times now, pointing to wire 1 as the one to act on. Display 0, light now red, wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue.

Deaf has relayed that Mute has consistently pointed to wire 1 across three rounds, which is strong, repeated confirmation of the same instruction — not a one-off ambiguous gesture. Combined with wire colors being stable (1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue) and only the light color changing, this looks like a consistent, deliberate signal from Mute (who has the manual) that wire 1 is correct to cut.

Given the repetition and consistency across multiple rounds, and that this is our only path to actually defusing the bomb, I'll proceed to cut wire 1.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
